rule_preceding: A flagged time-only marker (8:12-class) counts as PRECEDING an event only when the marker post's own harvest timestamp is strictly earlier than the event post's timestamp. Same-day or same-post accompaniment is POST-HOC (row 1 precedent: the Greenland 8:12 sample rode the announcement post itself and graded POST-HOC-UNVERIFIED). Bytes, not memory: both timestamps come from the harvest/ledger rows.
rule_window: A bare time-only marker declares a SAME-UTC-CALENDAR-DAY window: 00:00:00Z to 23:59:59Z of the day the marker post was made. A marker post that names an explicit interval (a date, 'this week', 'by <day>', 'the next habbening' with a named anchor) declares that interval instead; the explicit phrase always wins over this default. Sourcing, honest bounds: asekin's own on-file phrasing is date-anchored and event-noun-anchored (INTERPRETER_LAYER_20260918.md Yogasekin section: bio 'obtuse date phagger and follower of the habbenings'), and the ledger's only graded sample never declared a multi-day window for a time-only marker; the archived-posts sweep for an explicit interval phrase was ATTEMPTED and is UNRESOLVED this pass (web lane rate-limited; X archive not on file), so the same-day default is the conservative read and is re-openable by a byte-quoted interval phrase from his timeline.
rule_two_events: When N events land inside one marker's window, each grades independently against the same marker row. The marker grades HIT if any event inside the window meets the grading_bar (marker posted before the event, event inside the declared window); the graded event is named in the row and the others are recorded as companion events. One marker never grades twice as two HITs; it is one HIT with companions.
rule_preregistration: The window assignment must come from the marker post's bytes at row-filing time, before the event it will be graded against lands. A row whose window was assigned after the event landed grades POST-HOC-UNVERIFIED regardless of timing, which is the falsifier the brief pre-registered: a second graded row with a post-hoc-assigned window would make every future row gradeable HIT and void the ledger's base-rate use.
falsifier: a second graded row whose window was assigned after the event landed, which would make every future row gradeable HIT (verbatim from the B2-463 brief)
law_note: inherits the ledger's law_note: spookiness is data, wrongness is data, certainty is data; count activations against base rate over time
